children: Copper drops below $13,000 a metric ton as a stronger dollar, weaker sentiment around AI-related assets and concerns over Chinese demand weigh on the market. In early European trading, three-month futures on the LME are down 3.8% to $12,727.50 a ton, their lowest level since April. Weaker Chinese economic data has clouded the demand outlook for the base metal, which is used in electrical wiring and infrastructure. Meanwhile, growing concerns over the expansion of AI infrastructure after a Democratic sweep of Congress and management turmoil at leading chip maker Nvidia have further unsettled investors. Focus is now on the release of the Federal Reserve's October meeting minutes for clues on the outlook for interest rates, with more aggressive policy tightening widely expected. (giulia.petroni@wsj.com)
